seo.title: OpenPanel vs Umami: Product Analytics on Top of Web Stats
seo.description: Looking for an Umami alternative? OpenPanel offers deeper product analytics, user identification, and mobile SDKs while staying open source and privacy-first. Free to self-host.

hero.heading: OpenPanel vs Umami
hero.subheading: Love Umami's simplicity and privacy focus? OpenPanel adds user identification, mobile SDKs, session replay and detailed user profiles, while staying open source and cookie-free.

competitor.name: Umami Analytics
competitor.short_description: Privacy-focused, open-source web analytics with lightweight script and developer-friendly setup.

overview.title: Why consider OpenPanel over Umami?
paragraphs: Umami Analytics is a popular open-source web analytics tool known for its clean interface, lightweight script, and privacy-friendly design. It's a great option for developers who want simple, anonymous website metrics. But as your product grows beyond a simple website, Umami's anonymous-only model and lack of product analytics features become limiting.

OpenPanel builds on the same open-source, privacy-first foundation but adds the product analytics layer that Umami doesn't have. User identification lets you track logged-in users across sessions, while funnels, retention analysis, and cohort breakdowns help you understand how people actually use your product, not just that they visited your site.

Mobile app analytics is another area where OpenPanel pulls ahead. Umami is web-only with no native mobile SDKs, while OpenPanel has Swift (iOS), Kotlin (Android) and React Native SDKs. OpenPanel also has opt-in session replay and lets you compare variants by breaking any report down by a property.

OpenPanel is AGPL-3.0 licensed and Umami is MIT, both are open source and support self-hosting, so you won't sacrifice the open-source values that made Umami appealing. If you need to go beyond anonymous pageview counting and actually understand your users, OpenPanel is the natural upgrade from Umami.

summary_comparison.title: OpenPanel vs Umami: Which is right for you?
summary_comparison.intro: Both are open-source, privacy-focused analytics tools. Umami focuses on anonymous web analytics. OpenPanel adds user identification and product analytics.
summary_comparison.one_liner: Umami excels at anonymous web analytics; OpenPanel adds user identification, product analytics, session replay and mobile SDKs.

Teams that want session replay next to their events

highlights.title: Key differences at a glance
highlights.intro: Here's how OpenPanel and Umami compare on key factors.

items.label: User Identification
items.notes: OpenPanel lets you identify and track individual users across sessions. Umami intentionally anonymizes all data and doesn't support user identification to maximize privacy.

items.label: Mobile SDKs
items.notes: OpenPanel offers Swift, Kotlin and React Native SDKs. Umami is designed for web analytics and requires API calls for any server-side tracking.

items.label: Session replay
items.notes: OpenPanel records sessions when you enable it in the SDK config and keeps them 30 days. Umami has no session replay.

items.label: Free option
items.notes: Umami Cloud's Hobby plan is free for 100K events a month with 6 months of retention. OpenPanel Cloud has a 30-day trial then plans from $2.50/month; self-hosting is free with unlimited events.

items.label: Open Source License
items.notes: OpenPanel is AGPL-3.0; Umami is MIT, both are open source and self-hostable. Commercial use is allowed under both licenses.

feature_comparison.title: Feature comparison
feature_comparison.intro: Both are open source and privacy-focused, but with different depths of analytics capabilities.

features.name: Geographic Data
features.notes: Both offer country, region, and city-level data

features.name: Funnel Analysis
features.notes: Umami added funnels in 2023, supports URLs and custom events

features.name: User Profiles
features.notes: Umami intentionally doesn't track individual users

features.name: User Identification
features.notes: Umami has distinct ID but no true user identification

features.name: Session Replay
features.notes: OpenPanel replay is masked by default and kept 30 days

features.name: A/B Testing
features.notes: OpenPanel can break any report down by a variant property; neither tool has an experiment engine

features.name: Segments
features.notes: Umami v3 added saved filter segments

features.name: Email Reports
features.notes: OpenPanel sends a weekly insights digest and real-time alerts via Slack, Discord, webhook and in-app, not scheduled report emails. Umami email reports are cloud only.

features.name: Tracking Pixels
features.notes: Umami v3 added invisible tracking pixels for emails

features.name: Link Tracking
features.notes: Umami v3 added short URL link tracking. OpenPanel tracks outgoing link clicks but has no URL shortener.

features.name: No Consent Banner Required
features.notes: Both claim no consent needed for basic analytics

features.name: iOS SDK
features.notes: Umami is web-focused, no native mobile SDKs

features.name: Data Export
features.notes: Umami v3 added UI-based data export

technical_comparison.title: Technical comparison
technical_comparison.intro: For developers evaluating analytics tools, here's the technical breakdown.

items.label: SDK Size
items.openpanel: About 3 KB gzipped; session replay loads as a separate script only when enabled

items.label: Platforms
items.notes: Community SDKs exist for OpenPanel in PHP (Laravel) and Flutter. There is no Go SDK.

items.label: Open Source
items.notes: OpenPanel is AGPL-3.0; Umami is MIT. Both are open source. Umami has 23,000+ GitHub stars.

items.label: Self Hosting
items.openpanel: Docker Compose (ClickHouse, Postgres, Redis), one-command install script

pricing.title: Pricing comparison
pricing.intro: Umami has a free Hobby plan for small sites. OpenPanel has a 30-day trial, flat event-based pricing with every feature, and free unlimited self-hosting.

openpanel.model: Flat monthly by event volume, transparent
openpanel.description: Flat monthly tiers by event volume from $2.50 for 5,000 events ($20 for 100k, $90 for 1M), with a 30-day free trial and no free tier. All features on every tier. Self-host free with unlimited events.

competitor.model: Event-based with a free Hobby plan
competitor.description: Hobby: $0 for 100K events a month, 1 website, 6 months retention. Pro: $20/month for 1M events (then $0.00003 per event), up to 20 websites, 2 years retention. Business: $200/month for 10M events, unlimited websites, 5 years retention. Self-hosted Umami is free with no limits.

migration.title: Migrating from Umami to OpenPanel
migration.intro: Both use lightweight scripts with similar event tracking, and OpenPanel has a built-in Umami importer for your history.

steps.title: Install OpenPanel SDK
steps.description: Add the OpenPanel SDK to your application. Both scripts are small, so the transition is easy.

steps.title: Import your Umami history
steps.description: Export your data from Umami and upload the file in OpenPanel's Imports settings. Pageviews and events arrive with their original dates.

steps.title: Map Custom Events
steps.description: Umami custom events translate directly to OpenPanel. umami.track('signup', {plan: 'pro'}) becomes op.track('signup', {plan: 'pro'}).

steps.title: Add User Identification (New)
steps.description: Unlike Umami which is fully anonymous, OpenPanel supports user identification. Add op.identify() calls to unlock user profiles, retention by user, and cohort analysis.

steps.title: Recreate Funnels and Reports
steps.description: Set up your funnels in OpenPanel. You'll have access to additional product analytics features like user-level analysis that Umami doesn't provide.

steps.title: Remove Umami Script
steps.description: Once verified, remove the Umami tracking script. Both are cookie-free so no consent flow changes are needed.

sdk_compatibility.notes: Both use event-based tracking with similar APIs. umami.track() becomes op.track().

historical_data.notes: OpenPanel has a built-in Umami importer: export from Umami, upload the file under Settings > Imports, and watch the progress there.

use_cases.title: Where OpenPanel is a better fit than Umami
use_cases.intro: Choose OpenPanel when you need user identification, mobile SDKs, or A/B testing.

items.title: SaaS Products Needing User Identification
items.description: Umami anonymizes all visitors by design. If you need to track logged-in users, understand individual customer journeys, or analyze user-level retention, OpenPanel provides these capabilities while still respecting privacy.

items.title: Mobile App Analytics
items.description: Umami is designed for web analytics and doesn't offer native mobile SDKs. OpenPanel provides iOS (Swift), Android (Kotlin) and React Native SDKs with full product analytics capabilities.

items.title: Teams That Want Session Replay
items.description: Umami has no session replay. OpenPanel records sessions when you turn it on, masks text and inputs by default, and shows the recording next to the session's events.

items.title: Companies Building Data Pipelines
items.description: While Umami offers API access and data export, OpenPanel's ClickHouse backend is built for high-volume queries, and raw events can be exported to S3 or GCS every minute as JSONL.

items.title: Products Requiring Session-Level Analysis
items.description: Umami provides aggregate metrics but doesn't track individual sessions in detail. OpenPanel lets you analyze specific user sessions and behaviors.

faqs.title: Frequently asked questions
faqs.intro: Common questions about switching from Umami to OpenPanel.

items.question: Is OpenPanel as privacy-friendly as Umami?
items.answer: Both are cookie-free by default and GDPR compliant. The key difference is that OpenPanel allows optional user identification for product analytics, while Umami is strictly anonymous by design. You control whether to identify users in OpenPanel.

items.question: Why switch from Umami to OpenPanel?
items.answer: Teams typically switch when they need user identification, mobile SDKs or session replay. Umami excels at anonymous web analytics, but if you're building a product and need to understand individual user behavior across sessions, OpenPanel provides these capabilities.

items.question: How does Umami's free tier compare to OpenPanel?
items.answer: Umami Cloud's Hobby plan is free for 100K events a month on one website with 6 months of retention. OpenPanel Cloud has a 30-day free trial then plans from $2.50/month. Both self-hosted versions are free with no limits.

items.question: Which has the smaller tracking script?
items.answer: Umami's script is about 2 KB (1.5 KB gzipped) and OpenPanel's about 3 KB gzipped. Both are far smaller than Google Analytics (45 KB+) or Mixpanel.

items.question: Can Umami track mobile apps?
items.answer: Not with native SDKs. Umami is designed for web analytics and requires API calls for any non-browser tracking. OpenPanel offers Swift (iOS), Kotlin (Android) and React Native SDKs.

items.question: Does Umami support heatmaps or session replay?
items.answer: Umami has neither. OpenPanel has opt-in session replay (masked by default, kept 30 days) but no heatmaps.

items.question: How does self-hosting compare?
items.answer: Umami requires Docker with PostgreSQL (Node.js 18.18+). OpenPanel uses Docker Compose with ClickHouse, Postgres and Redis, and a one-command install script sets it up.

items.question: Is Umami or OpenPanel better for simple content websites?
items.answer: For simple blogs or content sites where you just need traffic stats without user identification, Umami's generous free tier and simplicity are excellent. For products, SaaS, or apps where you need to understand user behavior, OpenPanel's product analytics features provide more value.
